And you bring this up because what he's telling people is, you know, look, 'make peace with the ordinary'—is his own words—'shake hands with failure', sort of accept that this is a new normal. And your your reaction was interesting. It's like, wow, you know, a party-approved scholar is allowed to say this now.
transcript.zh: 但他今年春天出版了一本书，叫《无图之旅》。你之所以提到他，是因为他在书里对年轻人说，用他的原话说就是要“接纳平凡”、“与失败握手”，某种程度上是在让他们接受这就是新常态。你的反应很有意思，你会觉得：哇，体制认可的学者现在竟然可以公开讲这种话了。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: What does this tell you that this is now sayable? Just that the boom times are over, the Party kind of knows it, want people to, you know, make peace with the ordinary? And how does that fit in with this whole 'learn AI or get left behind' anxiety? Because, you know, these sound like very opposite pieces of advice aimed at the same generation.
transcript.zh: 这种话现在能够摆上台面，究竟说明了什么？是繁荣时代彻底落幕了，党内高层心知肚明，希望大家学会“安于平凡”？这又该如何与“不学AI就被淘汰”的焦虑自洽呢？因为这两套说辞听起来完全是背道而驰的，却又都指向同一代年轻人。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: One's telling you, okay, just you know, hey, this is the new normal. You're not going to necessarily lead a better life than your parents, but life is good, you know. You have waimai, you have you know lots of affordable things. And the other people are telling you, no, no, you still got to scramble to get ahead. You've got to keep up with the technology, and you better enroll in Shengcai Youdao, or you're screwed. It seems like two very different pieces of advice.
transcript.zh: 一种声音在告诉你：好吧，这就是新常态，你的生活未必能超越你的父辈，但当下日子也不差嘛，你有外卖，有各种物美价廉的消费品；而另一种声音却在对你大喊：不行不行，你必须拼命往前挤，必须跟上技术浪潮，赶紧报名“生财有道”，否则就全完了。这看起来完全是两种截然相反的人生建议。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: Yeah. So I got to know about Lian Si because he said he would say something like, our scholars, our job is no longer is no longer educate young people or encourage them to do things, but get closer to them and be sympathetic and be open. This is where he's coming from.
transcript.zh: 是的。我之所以关注到廉思，是因为他说过类似这样的话：作为学者，我们的工作已经不再是教育年轻人或给他们打鸡血，而是要走近他们、去共情他们，保持一种开放的心态。这就是他的立足点。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: So this Journey Without a Map, Wutu Zhi Lu, he interviewed 20 young people. It is essentially an ethnography for people who are...
transcript.zh: 在这本《无图之旅》中，他访谈了20位年轻人。这本质上是一部针对当下年轻人的民族志研究，记录那些正在……

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: In different provinces, doing different occupations, you know, including tech workers, including a worker who are, you know, working in the traditional manufacturing, including workers who are, you know, driving Didi or doing gig work. Yeah,送外卖. And a big part of me got pretty shocked is because it just it just simply, I just no longer sense this this default, absolutely convicted upward mobility that used to exist in Chinese society, like the Chinese society when I was growing up.
transcript.zh: 分布在不同省份、从事不同职业的人，包括科技行业从业者、传统制造业工人，还有开滴滴或做零工的人。是的，比如送外卖。让我深感震惊的一大原因是，我完全感受不到过去中国社会中那种理所当然、深信不疑的向上流动性了——那种在我成长岁月里曾普遍存在的社会流动预期。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: When I was growing up, like, the kind of message I got is, you know, I will have a better life than my parents. I will definitely have a better life than my parents. But the message I got from 《无图之旅》, from *Journey Without a Map*, is this renowned sociologist, the scholar, is trying to tell his peers to be sympathetic to the young people, as well as delivering the message to the young people saying, "You need to shake hands with failure, you need to make peace with the ordinary."
transcript.zh: 在我成长的过程中，我接收到的信息是：我的生活会比父母过得更好，绝对会比他们更好。但在《无图之旅》中，我读到的信息却是，这位著名的社会学学者一边呼吁同龄人理解包容年轻人，一边也在向年轻人喊话：“要学会与失败握手，学会甘于平凡。”

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: So I think it is there's certainly there's this vibe shift in such speech, in such discourse, in the book. So I I almost, you know, trying to to discern like is this Lian Si trying to tell the young people like, "It's okay to be doomed?" And at the same time, like many young people I met in Liangzhu, I met in Hangzhou, who are trying to host some AI events in their living rooms, who are trying to learn AI, to learn those skills, they are saying, "No, we don't want to listen to you."
transcript.zh: 我认为这本书里呈现的语调和话语体系确实发生了明显的风向转变。我甚至试图去探究：廉思是不是在委婉地告诉年轻人“认命也没关系”？但与此同时，我在良渚、在杭州遇到的很多年轻人，他们张罗着在客厅办 AI 沙龙、积极学习 AI 技能，他们会反驳说：“不，我们不想听你这一套。”

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: "You are, you know, the older generation who controls and monopolizes the resource, and you are the ones who prevented certain upward mobility that should belong to us." So, you know, I also sense this feeling where AI could be the tool for some true self-empowerment. And then I don't want to deny this sentiment.
transcript.zh: “你们是掌控并垄断了资源的年长一代，正是你们阻碍了本该属于我们的向上流动空间。”所以，我也真切感受到了另一种情绪——AI 或许能够成为实现真正自我赋能的工具。我并不想否认这种信念的存在。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, yeah. So this piece ends on the kind of idea of choicelessness and and coping, on what you you describe as sort of this crippled sense of agency. And then the *New Yorker* piece, which we're going to talk about now, you know, talks about AI offering people kind of a sense of agency, right? So this is the two are really to be read together. It's it's very interesting.
transcript.zh: 是的。因此那篇文章结尾落脚在一种“别无选择”与“勉力应对”的状态，也就是你所描述的那种受挫的能动性。而我们接下来要聊的《纽约客》特稿，讲的恰恰是 AI 似乎又赋予了人们某种能动性，对吧？这两篇文章确实应该对照着读，非常有意思。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I don't see those two things as necessarily in tension. I think you've just explained how these are kind of, you know, reconciled. Fortune-telling is what you focus on. A company called FateTell, it's a company in Liangzhu, right? This is a question I've been meaning to ask.
transcript.zh: 我不觉得这两者必然是对立的，你刚才恰好解释了它们是如何交织在一起的。你在那篇报道里重点关注了占卜算命，一家叫 FateTell 的公司，就在良渚，对吧？我一直很想问这个问题。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I've really wanted to ask somebody for some time, because I've seen a lot of this happening now. What is the legal status of all this? Because for a long time, the party's been quite aggressive about so-called, you know, fēngjiàn míxìn, you know, feudal superstition online.
transcript.zh: 我其实一直想找人问问这个问题，因为我注意到最近这类现象层出不穷。这一切在法律层面上究竟算什么性质？毕竟长期以来，党对网络上所谓的“封建迷信”一直打击得相当严厉。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: On Taobao, you can't search for fortune-telling. City governments have put out notices telling people not to seek comfort in fortune-telling. And just this year, there were new rules about clergy using AI, right?
transcript.zh: 在淘宝上你搜不到算命服务；各地市政府也纷纷发文，告诫大家不要通过算命寻求心理慰藉；就在今年，还出台了针对宗教神职人员使用AI的新规，对吧？

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: FateTell has hundreds of thousands of users, a paid tier. You cite an AI fortune-telling industry worth 120 billion yuan in your piece. How does a company like that operate out in the open?
transcript.zh: 但FateTell却拥有数十万用户，还推出了付费档次。你在文章中援引的数据显示，AI算命产业的产值高达1200亿元。这样一家公司是怎么做到公开展业的？

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I mean, was something lifted? Is there a change of regulations that I'm not aware of? Is this a gray zone? Is there a framing that they can use, you know, calling it cultural heritage or Eastern wisdom that makes it somehow acceptable to the authorities, where just like Western horoscopes might not be? How does this work?
transcript.zh: 我的意思是，某些限制被放开了吗？还是有我不知道的法规变动？这算是一个灰色地带吗？他们是不是有一套话语包装，比如冠以“传统文化遗产”或“东方智慧”之名，从而让官方默许，而像西方星座占卜可能就享受不到这种待遇？这背后到底是怎么运作的？

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: I do find this confusing as well. One thing that's pretty shocking to me is the past two years when I go back to China and chat with my friends or younger people, I just realize this entire healing industry, this entire fortune-telling industry is just everywhere.
transcript.zh: 我也觉得这挺让人看不懂的。过去两年里让我非常震惊的一点是，当我回到中国和朋友们或者年轻人聊天时，我才发现整个疗愈产业、整个算命行业简直无处不在。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: And all the younger girls, you know, I hang out with, let's say in Shanghai, are all using tarot cards to read about their career, to read about their finance, to read about their relationship. It is just so out there.
transcript.zh: 我在上海一起玩的所有年轻女孩，全都在用塔罗牌来测算她们的事业、财务和感情状况。这种现象简直太普遍、太公开了。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: I don't even know if it could be regulated. When I was visiting Shenzhen, for example, I was visiting this hardware store. Outside, there was this giant machine that plays... it almost like a slot machine you can see in Las Vegas, but much bigger.
transcript.zh: 我甚至不知道这到底能不能管得过来。比如我去深圳的时候，逛了一家五金店。外面放着一台巨大的机器，正在播放……它有点像你在拉斯维加斯能见到的老虎机，但体型要大得多。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: And then the screen just shows this tarot pattern and you can interact with the machine, and then many people are lining up to interact with the machine. So those things are just out there on the street.
transcript.zh: 屏幕上显示出塔罗牌的图案，你可以和这台机器互动，而且有很多人在排队等着玩。所以这类东西在大街上随处可见。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: And when I was visiting Liangzhu, it's a very similar feeling. You see a bunch of stores selling crystals. You see this tarot reading signs where it seems to be a proper business. You see many shops are providing the healing services.
transcript.zh: 我去良渚的时候也是非常相似的感觉。你会看到一堆卖水晶的店铺，能看到塔罗占卜的招牌，看起来完全是正规的营生，你还能看到很多店铺在提供疗愈服务。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: And when I was visiting in January, I went to the Jade Bird Land, which is the main commercial district in Liangzhu. They have this official village calendar, and many of those events have something to do with spirituality.
transcript.zh: 今年一月份我去走访时，去了玉鸟集，那是良渚的核心商业街区。他们有一份官方发布的村落活动日历，上面的很多活动都与灵修身心灵有关。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: For example, how to dress for luck according to the I Ching philosophy, the Heart Sutra reading session.
transcript.zh: 比如，如何根据《易经》哲学穿搭转运，还有《心经》诵读会等等。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: And many events are just like that. It's just really out there, so...
transcript.zh: 很多活动就是这种风格，真的很离奇超脱，所以……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: This place is starting to sound like Sedona, Arizona, I don't know if you've ever been there.
transcript.zh: 这地方听起来越来越像亚利桑那州的塞多纳（Sedona）了，不知道你去过没有。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: Yeah, it is Sedona. It is China's Sedona! I was like, is this the New Age-y town in China, in Liangzhu? Because it makes a lot of sense, because Liangzhu has certain shamanic elements in it, right? Because the Liangzhu ruins was there, there are people practicing those worship to...
transcript.zh: 没错，它就是塞多纳，就是中国的塞多纳！我当时就想，良渚难道是中国的“新时代”（New Age）小镇吗？因为这完全说得通：良渚本身就带有某种萨满巫觋文化元素，对吧？毕竟良渚遗址就在那里，古代先民在那里进行祭祀崇拜……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah. They were doing astrology, right? Yeah.
transcript.zh: 对，他们当时还会观星占星，对吧？是的。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: Yeah, they were doing astrology back then. There are a lot of mystical symbols on those jade artifacts that symbolizes the shamanic status of some ruler in the Liangzhu ancestral culture, yeah.
transcript.zh: 是的，他们那时候就懂得观象。在那些出土的玉器上有很多神秘符号，象征着良渚先祖文化中某些统治者的巫觋神权地位，确实如此。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Well, so let's talk about this company. And what's his name, is it Levi or Levy? How does he pronounce it?
transcript.zh: 好，那我们来聊聊这家公司。还有那个创始人的名字，是念 Levi 还是 Levy？他自己怎么发音？

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: Levy. I think it's Levy, yeah. Okay, yeah.
transcript.zh: Levy。我想是念 Levy，对。好的。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So let's talk about this guy, Levy. He was the founder of FateTell. It's based on the BaZi. BaZi are, literally the "eight figures", you know, the numbers of the date and time of your birth, right? So it's a fortune-telling app, it's at the center of your piece.
transcript.zh: 那我们就来聊聊这位叫 Levy 的人。他是 FateTell 的创始人，这款产品以“八字”为基础。八字字面意思就是八个字，也就是你出生的年月日时对应的天干地支，对吧？所以这是一款算命 App，也是你报道的核心。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: This guy nearly became a Daoist monk, in his own telling. He worked at ByteDance. He actually almost—I guess he's a big sci-fi fan, he's a big Dune fan because he almost named his company Muad'Dib after Paul Atreides, you know, the guy that Timothée Chalamet plays in the Dune movies.
transcript.zh: 据他自己说，他差点出家当了道士。他曾在字节跳动工作过。实际上他差点——我猜他是个超级科幻迷，非常喜欢《沙丘》（Dune），因为他差点把公司命名为穆阿迪布（Muad'Dib），也就是保罗·厄崔迪的名字，就是甜茶在《沙丘》电影里演的那个角色。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: He's cast the BaZi of all these famous Western tech leaders. So I guess you cite one, you say Sam Altman comes off as a mercenary accountant, which is kind of a funny thing.
transcript.zh: 他给西方所有著名的科技领袖都排过八字。你在文章里引用了一个，说山姆·奥特曼（Sam Altman）的八字排出来像个市侩的账房先生，这还挺搞笑的。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: Yeah.
transcript.zh: 是的。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: But yeah, I'm wondering, do you have other—did he do one on Dario, or on Jensen, or...?
transcript.zh: 不过话说回来，我想知道你还知道别的吗——他有没有给 Dario（Anthropic 创始人）或者黄仁勋排过？

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: Oh, he mentioned... So there's one thing that I didn't really reveal in the article is they actually has an in-house BaZi master who has this prophetic power to not just calculating other people's BaZi, but also, you know, trying to calculate the BaZi for the celebrities, for the US president, to predict the future financial trends.
transcript.zh: 噢，他提过……我在文章里其实没完全写出来的一点是，他们团队内部其实有一位常驻的八字大师。这位大师有一种预测神通，不仅能算普通人的八字，还会去推算各路名流、甚至美国总统的八字，以此来预测未来的宏观金融走势。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: Yeah, so he shared some with me, but I couldn't remember. But I just remember clearly that he thinks Sam Altman is a "suànzhàng de" (accountant), or someone like, you know, is one of those minor people...
transcript.zh: 对，他跟我分享过一些，但我记不太清了。我只清楚记得，他觉得山姆·奥特曼就是个“算账的”，或者类似于那种无足轻重的小角色……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: A bean counter, yeah.
transcript.zh: 一个精打细算的账房先生，对。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: Yeah, a bean counter. Yeah, yeah, yeah. So it's really hilarious. And Levy is a founder, I think, has both this business savviness as well as a great storytelling abilities, but also he's deeply, deeply believed in the BaZi cosmology.
transcript.zh: 对，就是个账房先生，哈哈。所以真的特别搞笑。而 Levy 这个创始人，我认为他既有极高的商业精明度，又极擅长讲故事，但与此同时，他又打心底里深信八字的宇宙观。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: So I think one of the most surreal experiences I was hanging out with the FateTell team was we were in a dinner. So we were in a dinner together...
transcript.zh: 所以我觉得和 FateTell 团队相处时最超现实的经历之一，是有一次我们一起吃晚饭。当时我们一桌人正在聚餐……

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: And their fortune-telling master was also among our dinner. And you just see the entire conversation was about how to optimize your BaZi with the year of Fire Horse elements. How do you avoid certain life atrocities? How do you maximize your luck?
transcript.zh: 他们的算命大师也和我们一起吃了晚饭。你会发现整场谈话都在讨论如何根据“丙午火马年”的五行来优化八字。怎样避开人生的大灾大难？怎样让自己的运势最大化？

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: You know, the COO of FateTell, her name is Sally, she moved her house from one place to a community that's near the hospital, because the master kind of warned him that, "You are going to the hospital a lot this year." And she indeed been going to the hospital a lot.
transcript.zh: FateTell 的首席运营官 Sally，甚至把家从原来的地方搬到了医院附近的小区，因为大师警告她说：“你今年会频繁跑医院。”而事实证明，她确实经常去医院。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Oh, Christ. Yeah, self-fulfilling. Let me play the skeptic here for just a minute and tie this back to the other piece, because Levy will tell you—and he does in the piece, you quote him—saying that the I Ching is humanity's first statistical decision model, and a model that gets better at math and coding must therefore get better at reading fate.
transcript.zh: 天呐。是啊，自我实现的预言。让我在这里扮演一下怀疑论者，顺便把这个话题和你另一篇文章联系起来。因为 Levy 会告诉你——你在报道中也引用了他的话——他说《易经》是人类历史上第一个统计决策模型，既然模型越来越擅长数学和代码，那它必然也会越来越擅长算命。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: But, come on. I wonder whether there isn't a certain cynicism underlying all of this stuff. Knowing there's a reporter writing about them for The New Yorker there, they're going to put on a big show. They're going to bring the BaZi master to dinner. They're going to talk only about that, they're going to seem earnest about it. But I wonder if there isn't a certain...
transcript.zh: 但是，拜托。我怀疑这一切背后是不是存在某种犬儒主义。知道现场有位《纽约客》的记者在写他们，他们当然得做足全套戏码。他们把八字大师请来共进晚餐，满嘴聊的都是这些，显得无比虔诚。但我怀疑这背后难道就没有某种……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I don't know, come on. The people building FateTell know perfectly well that augury and astrology have nothing whatsoever to do with the math and the engineering that make a large language model work, right? I mean, come on.
transcript.zh: 我都不知道该怎么说，算了吧。开发 FateTell 的人心里门儿清：占卜和星盘跟支撑大语言模型运转的数学和工程原理根本没有半毛钱关系，对吧？我是说，得了吧。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I'm pretty sure they do, though, have a very old understanding of human gullibility. You got a market of people who are deeply anxious about a future that, ironically, AI itself is making uncertain, right? The anxiety is coming from AI, so let's use that same thing, AI, to sell to them.
transcript.zh: 不过我敢肯定，他们非常懂得如何利用人类根深蒂固的盲信弱点。面前有一整个市场的受众，对未来充满极度焦虑，而讽刺的是，这恰恰是 AI 本身带来的不确定性，对吧？焦虑因 AI 而起，那干脆就用 AI 这个同款产品来收割他们。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I don't think it's that different from Mr. Tree selling 3,000-yuan memberships to a security guard. I mean, the I Ching being 3,000 years old doesn't change the nature of the transaction. I see lots of parallels to—and I think it's obvious, and you saw them, too...
transcript.zh: 我觉得这跟那个“树先生”向保安兜售 3000 元的会员课程没什么两样。《易经》哪怕有三千年历史，也改变不了这种交易的本质。我看到了很多相似之处——而且我觉得很明显，你也看出来了……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I don't know if you're familiar with the Bay Area where you live in in the early '70s, you know, the whole Whole Earth Catalog years, Stewart Brand. Ken Kesey, the Merry Pranksters, he's on the bus with them. He puts out this compendium, and it's very hippie in the same way, sort of high-tech hippie, right? Geodesic domes, and the I Ching.
transcript.zh: 我不知道你熟不熟悉你现在居住的湾区在 70 年代初的景象，就是《全球概览》（Whole Earth Catalog）风靡的年代，Stewart Brand。还有 Ken Kesey 和他的“快乐恶作剧者”，他和他们一起在巴士上巡游。他出版了那本大百科，同样充满了嬉皮色彩，属于某种“高科技嬉皮”，对吧？测地线穹顶，还有《易经》。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So I guess, aren't they kind of like too deliberately kind of recreating this same thing? And I don't know, it just, something feels wrong to me about this.
transcript.zh: 所以我觉得，他们是不是有点太刻意地在复刻同一套东西了？我不知道，这总让我感觉哪里有点不对劲。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: I think this New Age-y...
transcript.zh: 我觉得这种新时代（New Age）风格的……

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: movement in Liangzhu is an imported New Age-y movement from part of the Western world. I think the version of I Ching, the version of fortune-telling, and the version of the Eastern philosophy is actually first sort of influenced, impacted the West in the counterculture age.
transcript.zh: 良渚的这股风潮，实际上是从西方世界某些地区输入进来的新时代运动（New Age）。我认为，那里的易经版本、算命版本以及东方哲学版本，最初是在反文化运动时期影响了西方。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: And then later, it was sort of repackaged and imported back to China. So the version of the Chinese New Age-y I saw in Liangzhu is actually a pretty much Westernized, changed New Age practice.
transcript.zh: 随后它被重新包装，又回流并逆向输入回了中国。所以我在良渚看到的这种中国式“新时代”风潮，本质上是高度西方化、被改造过的新时代实践。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: And then I do think Livvy himself is a great marketer. You know, he's absolutely very, very smart and then exactly knows how to tell his story. Initially, when I was hanging out with the Liangzhu vibe coders, with the Liangzhu tech people, I probably met like 50, 60 of them.
transcript.zh: 而且我认为Livvy本人是个极佳的营销高手。他非常非常聪明，深谙如何讲好自己的故事。起初，当我和良渚的“氛围编码”（vibe-coding）群体、那里的科技从业者打交道时，我大概接触了五六十个人。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: And Livvy was one of the last batch of people I got to know, but later he became my character just because he's really compelling, you know. He often tells me all these interesting practices he's doing.
transcript.zh: Livvy是我认识的最后一批人之一，但他后来成了我文章里的主角，完全是因为他这个人太引人注目了。他经常跟我讲他正在做的那些有趣实践。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: And he's telling me this hardware he's trying to do is because, you know, if you wanted to have this fortune-telling to be more accurate, you need to build this psychic connection with actual objects. That's why he's building hardware.
transcript.zh: 他跟我说他想做硬件，是因为如果你想让算命更准确，就必须和实体物品建立某种通灵/心灵感应联结。这就是他做硬件的原因。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: So, you know, he has many ways of selling his company in a compelling way. And he's also a media figure that's been reported by many tech medias in China. So I don't want to deny that. I do think Livvy is also deeply, deeply infused in this BaZi cosmology.
transcript.zh: 所以你看，他有很多极具说服力的方式来包装推销自己的公司。他本身也是个媒体红人，被很多国内科技媒体报道过。所以我不否认这一点。我确实觉得Livvy自己也深深沉浸在这套八字宇宙观里。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: Like one, after the article published, Livvy posted on social media and he says, "Liangzhu indeed has great feng shui. Our company became part of The New Yorker report." So I think this is maybe his genuine reaction.
transcript.zh: 比如，文章发表后，Livvy在社交媒体上发帖说：“良渚的风水确实好，我们公司都登上了《纽约客》的报道。”所以我觉得这也许就是他的真实反应。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: And then, not just Livvy is doing fortune-telling applications. It's like a lot of other people in Liangzhu I met are also doing some, you know, purple star map reading, tarot reading. They're all building these AI fortune-telling applications.
transcript.zh: 而且，不仅是Livvy在做算命应用。我在良渚遇到的很多其他人也都在做紫微斗数看盘、塔罗牌占卜。他们全都在开发这类AI算命应用。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So when you were, you know, you're in this room at FateTell party, the COO is reading your chart. Do you see around you in these people, people who believe this, people who've found a product, or people who've just stopped being able to tell the difference between belief and product? I mean, that's...
transcript.zh: 所以当你置身于FateTell聚会的那个房间里，COO在给你看命盘时，你看到身边的这些人，是真正坚信这一套的人，是找到了产品方向的人，还是已经彻底分不清信仰与产品之间区别的人？我的意思是，那简直……

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: The thing is, one thing I do want to convince the readers is they do believe in it. It is no joke. Like during the opening day, it is also the beginning of certain Buddhist...
transcript.zh: 问题的关键在于，我非常想让读者明白的一点是：他们是真信。这不是开玩笑。比如在开幕日那天，正好也是某个佛教……

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: spiritual month. And then, during this month, you can—it is a good opportunity to practice fasting, to prac—to to practice differ—different a variety of things. And, one of the hardware engineers—his name is Feicai. He's really funny guy. He loves to talk, he's extremely talkative.
transcript.zh: 灵修月。在这个月里，你可以……这是个辟谷的好机会，可以练习各种各样的事情。其中一位硬件工程师叫肥柴，他是个特别有意思的人，超级爱说话，非常健谈。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: And then, we were chatting so much the day before. And, during the office opening party, at the beginning of this Buddhist and spiritual month, he decided to do a speech fasting. It means he don't—he will not talk for two weeks.
transcript.zh: 我们前一天还聊得热火朝天。结果在办公室开业派对上，恰逢这个佛教灵修月的开始，他决定进行“禁语”。也就是说，他接下来的两周内都不会开口说话。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: And, and then, he was really serious about it. So, when I met him, he was excited to to to wave to me, but he typed it on the phone and showed it to me, said, "Only ask me yes or no questions." You know, that was some real practice. And those people are genuinely convicted.
transcript.zh: 而且他是非常认真的。当我见到他时，他很兴奋地朝我招手，但他在手机上打字给我看，上面写着：“请只问我‘是’或‘否’的问题。”你看，这可是动真格的修行，这些人是真的深信不疑。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: And then, when they are hiring new people, they will do this compatibility. Um, they're not—I don't think they they they can fake the whole thing in front of me.
transcript.zh: 他们在招新人的时候，还会去合八字看是否契合。他们不是在……我觉得他们不可能在我面前把整套东西全演出来。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Is there—is that legal? Can you can you discriminate based on on superstition? I wonder. I mean, and and you know, what you just said is is kind of interesting. Yeah, let's let's chalk another one up for the Chinese syncretism.
transcript.zh: 这……这合法吗？你能根据这种迷信来搞歧视吗？我很好奇。不过，你刚才说的确实挺有意思的。得，这又得算在中国式融通的账上了。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Because, you know, the I Ching was compiled, what, 500 years, give or take, before the birth of of the Shakyamuni Gautama Buddha. Uh and, you know, so let's Yeah, let's throw in a mishmash of Buddhist spiritual months as well as I Ching practices as well as every grab bag of superstitious nonsense that we can lay hold of, but anyway.
transcript.zh: 因为《易经》成书大概比释迦牟尼佛祖降生还要早个五百年左右。所以干脆把佛教的灵修月、《易经》的玄学实践，再加上随手能抓来的一切迷信大杂烩全搅和在一起，但不管怎么说吧……

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: Yeah. Yeah. I would randomly throw—I would randomly gave them some information about my bazi, and all of them just like listened so carefully and seriously. And like it's almost like they're trying to build a some mental model about me.
transcript.zh: 是的。我当时随口跟他们透露了一点我自己的八字信息，他们全都听得特别认真、格外严肃。就好像他们正试图在脑海中为我建立某种认知模型一样。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: And then, this random piece of information about my bazi became another important factor they're trying to to put in. So, yeah, they're they're quite serious about this. This is just That's why this this whole thing is really fascinating, right?
transcript.zh: 然后关于我八字的这一条零散信息，就成了他们试图纳入模型的另一个关键要素。所以说，他们对这套东西是非常当真的。正因如此，整件事情才显得格外耐人寻味，不是吗？

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah. I mean, I I can't I cannot contain my contempt for this. I'm sorry. Let's talk about what happens, though, when the local government falls in love with a scene like this.
transcript.zh: 确实。不过抱歉，我实在掩饰不住自己对这种事的鄙夷。但咱们还是聊聊看，当地方政府看中并介入这样一个生态时，会发生什么吧。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Because, you know, we've seen this happen before. You know, there's the Seeker 1 incubator with its "new quality productive forces" boilerplate that you talk about. There's Master Qi, you know, he's standing next to this party official at the ribbon cutting.
transcript.zh: 因为我们以前见过太多这种场景了。比如你文章里提到的“良渚寻客一号”孵化器，满嘴套用“新质生产力”的官方官样套话；还有七爷，在剪彩仪式上就并排站在党委干部身旁。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Uh there's this tech influencer that you talk about named Toolatrix uh who who runs a weekly gathering called Crazy Thursday. And I I'm glad that you noted the origins in KFC online promotions for Crazy Thursday.
transcript.zh: 还有你写到的那位网名叫“工具乐器”（Toolatrix）的科技网红，他每周组织一场名为“疯狂星期四”的聚会。我很欣慰你指出了“疯狂星期四”其实源自肯德基的线上促销文案。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Again, Chinese syncretism. You know, take it from anywhere you can, right? Even if it's fast food, Western fast food. But, you know, there's other people who are scouting the next town already because they think that that Liangzhu only has maybe a couple of years left. I I I've seen how this this happens, right? We've seen like, you know, 798 or Songzhuang.
transcript.zh: 这又是中国式的兼收并蓄——逮着什么用什么，哪怕是洋快餐的梗也不例外。但与此同时，已经有人在物色下一个落脚的小镇了，因为他们觉得良渚的好日子大概也就剩个一两年了。这种戏码我见得太多了，就像当年的798艺术区或者宋庄艺术村那样。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: In Beijing or maybe Dali, I mean, they sort of become a fad for a little while. People all go there and then they, you know, it gets kind of enshittified somehow and then everyone leaves.
transcript.zh: 在北京，或者在大理。这类地方往往会风靡一时，大家都蜂拥而至，然后不知怎的就体验变差、走向劣化，接着所有人又都散了。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: Yeah. I mean, unfortunately, I think by the time the article is published, I think Liangzhu's peak is, in fact, over. It's because the place is already somewhat institutionalized.
transcript.zh: 是的。遗憾的是，我觉得等到这篇文章发表的时候，良渚的巅峰期其实已经过去了。因为这个地方在某种程度上已经被收编、体制化了。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: So when I was chatting with another friend in Shanghai, he's a tech company CEO, and I also mentioned I was like, "I'm working on something about Liangzhu." He says, "Oh, isn't this place is already like sort of boring? Became boring again?"
transcript.zh: 之前我和上海的一位朋友聊天，他是一家科技公司的CEO。我随口提到：“我最近在写一篇关于良渚的稿子。”他直接说：“啊？那地方不是已经挺无聊的了吗？又变得没劲了吧？”

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: You know, because the peak was the post-COVID two years. And now Liangzhu has been seen as a bunch of, you know, some people are more or less grifty, and some people are just... It's just not organic anymore, because the local government are trying to absorb and institutionalize this organic scene.
transcript.zh: 因为良渚最火的是疫情后的那两年。现在的良渚给人的感觉是，混进去了不少捞快钱的投机客，还有些人纯粹是……总之它不再有那种自发生长的野生感了。因为当地政府正试图把这种自发的民间生态收编并体制化。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: That's why there are district bureaus would go to the quote-unquote founder of "Crazy Thursday", this tech gathering event, saying, "Can you change your location from gathering in a coffee shop to our newly built office space? We will provide this and that to you."
transcript.zh: 这也是为什么会有区级招商部门找上“疯狂星期四”这一科技沙龙的所谓发起人，跟他们说：“你们能不能别在咖啡馆聚了，搬到我们新建的办公园区去？我们给你们提供各种补贴和扶持。”

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: And then, you know, he ended up refusing, because when you change the organic scene to somewhere else has some other purposes, the energy, this originality is gone.
transcript.zh: 结果他给拒绝了。因为一旦你把这种自发原生的小圈子搬到带着其他功利目的的地方，那种活力、那种原创的灵气就荡然无存了。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: And, you know, Liangzhu used to be the place where people in Shanghai, in Beijing, in Shenzhen, even Silicon Valley would fly over to to learn about things, to learn about this some new trends, especially during the first two years of of of AI boom, where the consumer apps was the point of growth.
transcript.zh: 要知道，良渚曾经是上海、北京、深圳甚至硅谷的人都会特地飞过来取经的地方，大家来这里捕捉新趋势，尤其是在这轮AI热潮最初的两年里，当时C端应用正是核心增长点。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: But now, unfortunately, I think Liangzhu became is not cool anymore, in a sense. And similar to some other local governments, like local government in Huangshan, local government in Anji, even the local government of, yeah, some like coastal cities, they are all trying to attract quote-unquote "vibe coders" or one-person companies.
transcript.zh: 但很遗憾，现在的良渚在某种意义上已经“不酷”了。而且国内其他一些地方政府，比如黄山、安吉，甚至某些沿海城市的政府，现在都在极力招揽所谓的“氛围写码”独立开发者或者超级个体、一人公司。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Of course they are. [laughter]
transcript.zh: 他们肯定会这么干。[笑]

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: Yeah, this seems to be the slogan to attract and to correspond to the "AI Plus" plan, to correspond with the trend of attracting more people who are building things with the new quality productivity force, AI, right?
transcript.zh: 没错，这似乎成了招商引资的标准口号，用来呼应国家层面的“人工智能+”行动，顺应借由新质生产力——也就是AI——来吸引更多弄潮儿的浪潮，对吧？

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: And then, you know, and all those local governments are trying to find the next new thing to attract more people. And then, Liangzhu government is one of the very, very tech-savvy governments. It's the Yuhang government, and the Yuhang government has many competitors around it. So, when I was visiting Liangzhu, those off...
transcript.zh: 所有这些地方政府都在试图寻找下一个新风口来聚拢人才。而良渚背后其实是一个对科技非常敏感的政府，也就是余杭区政府。余杭周边面临着很多强劲的竞争对手。所以当我去良渚走访时，那些官办……

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: Official tech incubators, the recruiters are very savvy. You know, they got my WeChat, they invited me to the Liangzhu community, officially run community, and they're trying to ask me if I want to build a company there. When I was only chatting with them for 10 minutes, they immediately talked...
transcript.zh: 官方的科技孵化器，那些招商人员非常精明。他们加了我的微信，邀请我加入良渚的社群——官方运营的社群，还一直问我想不想在那儿开公司。我才跟他们聊了十分钟，他们就立刻开始谈……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Well, you're an OPC, right? You're running a Substack.
transcript.zh: 好吧，你就是个一人公司（OPC），对吧？你在运营自己的Substack专栏。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: I'm an OPC. I'm an OPC, yeah.
transcript.zh: 我就是一个一人公司。我就是，没错。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I'm an OPC. I've got a podcast.
transcript.zh: 我也是一人公司。我做着一档播客。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: We are all OPCs.
transcript.zh: 我们都是一人公司。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah. I'm down with OPC.
transcript.zh: 对。我很赞同一人公司的概念。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: Yeah, I was immediately being given a lot of information of how to register a company there, how to pay this, you know, social security there, and what kind of benefits I can get from the Liangzhu government in terms of the amount of compute, the amount of token, and some sort of subsidies. So yeah, I was immediately being recruited, just simply because, you know, those governments, they crave growth, they crave young people, they crave...
transcript.zh: 对，我立刻就收到了大量信息，教我怎么在那儿注册公司，怎么在那儿交社保，以及能从良渚政府那里拿到什么样的优惠政策——比如多少算力额度、多少Token额度，还有各种补贴。所以说，我立刻就成了他们招揽的对象，纯粹就是因为当地政府极度渴求增长，极度渴求年轻人，极度渴求……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: They probably cast your BaZi and figured you'd be a good fit.
transcript.zh: 他们可能还排了你的八字，觉得你特别合适。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: Yeah.
transcript.zh: 是啊。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Before we wind up here, let me put the big Western question to you very directly, because you are the person who can actually answer it. Is the idea that Chinese people are cavalier about AI safety, that they basically don't care about or don't believe in the existential risks—is that a fair characterization? What are people in these rooms that you've been in actually worried about when it comes to AI? Is risk being talked about at all, maybe just in a vocabulary that we're not listening for or attuned to?
transcript.zh: 在我们结束之前，让我非常直接地向你提出那个西方最为关注的核心问题，因为你正是那个能给出真正答案的人。有一种观点认为，中国人对人工智能安全不以为意，基本上不在乎甚至不相信所谓的存在性风险——这种定性公允吗？在人工智能方面，你所接触过的那些圈子里的人究竟在担忧什么？大家到底有没有在谈论风险，还是说只是用了一种我们未曾留心、或尚未习惯的语汇？

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: This is a great question. My understanding is, many AI researchers I talked to worked in the Chinese AI labs, they don't think safety issues are on their lane. They believe certain safety issues are the responsibility for the government, and then they definitely don't want to take the job from the government. So this is like one dimension.
transcript.zh: 问得太好了。我的理解是，我接触过的许多在中国人工智能实验室工作的AI研究员，他们并不认为安全问题是自己的职责范畴。他们觉得某些安全问题属于政府的管辖责任，而且他们绝对不想去越俎代庖。所以这是其中的一个维度。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: And the second point is often that, so you know that Silicon Valley, for example OpenAI, they would do this experiment of trying to mobilize a lot of agents to tackle a very long and complex question, and that ended up causing something like the Hugging Face incident. Doing such experiment is very costly, and compared to the capital that the Silicon Valley AI labs have versus the capital of a Chinese AI lab could mobilize, the Chinese companies sometimes cannot really afford to do such frontier risky experiment to test out the capability.
transcript.zh: 第二点往往在于，你看硅谷那边，比如OpenAI，他们会去做这样的实验：调动大量智能体（Agent）去攻关一个极长、极其复杂的问题，结果引发了类似Hugging Face事件那样的情况。做这种实验成本极高，而且对比硅谷AI实验室所拥有的资本与中国AI实验室所能调动的资本，中国企业有时根本承担不起去做这种前沿且高风险的实验来测试模型的能力极限。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: So, I guess what I'm trying to say is, first, the Chinese AI companies, they do not really...
transcript.zh: 所以，我想表达的是，首先，中国的人工智能企业并没有真正……

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: doing things that's as dangerous and frontier as their Silicon Valley counterpart. And second, they're just very practical about this. It's because doing such experiment is costly and they have scarce capital, they have scarce compute.
transcript.zh: 去做像硅谷同行那样危险且处于最前沿的事情。其次，他们在这方面非常务实。因为做这类实验成本高昂，而他们的资金很紧缺，算力也非常匮乏。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: And all they want to do is focus on improving the benchmarks, focus on improving the model capabilities so they can have relatively good return. Because those companies actually have a lot of pressure to generate wealth for the local economy.
transcript.zh: 他们真正想做的，就是集中精力刷榜提升基准测试表现，提升模型能力，从而获得相对不错的回报。因为这些公司实际上背负着为地方经济创造财富的巨大压力。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: They also, you know, in a sense, they are a bunch of very highly educated STEM people, the successors of gaokao. And improving benchmark is a very natural thing to them, because it is essentially an optimization problem rather than an open-ended question.
transcript.zh: 而且在某种程度上，他们是一群受过高等教育的理工科精英，是高考体系的胜出者。提升跑分基准对他们来说是一件顺理成章的事，因为这本质上是一个优化问题，而不是一个开放式命题。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: I guess the final reason why I would argue that Chinese AI labs are less concerned about AI safety is because dealing with AI safety is an endless, is a very complex and open-ended question, and it's costly.
transcript.zh: 我觉得中国AI实验室不太关注AI安全的最后一个原因，在于处理AI安全是一个无休止、极其复杂且开放性的问题，而且代价高昂。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: So many AI researchers are like, if Sam Altman, Elon Musk, and Dario are thinking about this, why am I here to worry about that? Or I can just adopt their methodology of safety practices to our company rather than figure this out from zero to one.
transcript.zh: 所以很多AI研究员的想法是：既然Sam Altman、Elon Musk和Dario都在思考这些，我又何必操心呢？或者我们直接把他们的安全实践方法套用到自己公司就行了，没必要从零到一去重新琢磨。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: Yeah, I think it is a mixture of pragmatism. There's a mixture of, you know, also the trust of state capacity, right? It's really hard for Chinese government to believe something lives in the computer could be potentially dangerous.
transcript.zh: 是的，我觉得这既是一种实用主义，同时也混杂着对国家治理能力的信任，对吧？中国政府其实很难相信存活在电脑里的东西会具有潜在危险。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: Of course, you know, I'm not saying Chinese government don't care about cybersecurity. But what I say is the government has a really strong control of the physical reality, of the physical world. So it's really hard to really convince them that this could be catastrophic.
transcript.zh: 当然，我不是说中国政府不在乎网络安全。但我想说的是，政府对物理现实、对实体世界有着极强的控制力。所以很难真正说服他们这可能会引发灾难性后果。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I got it. Yeah. So they don't think it's really their job because it's the government's job. I mean, worrying about things like AI safety, that's something they're happy to hand off to the government.
transcript.zh: 我懂了，是的。所以他们觉得这不是自己的本职工作，因为那是政府的事。我是说，操心AI安全这类事情，他们很乐意甩手推给政府。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: They don't engage in these sorts of wild sandbox experiments where they sick tons of agents on very, very difficult problems, and then, you know, tell these agents they're going to be benchmarked and thus incentivize them to do naughty things.
transcript.zh: 他们不会去搞那种天马行空的沙盒实验，把大批智能体放出去解决极难的问题，然后告诉它们会进行评测，从而刺激它们做出越轨举动。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And yeah, and basically they think they can adopt whatever best practices come out of these labs that are thinking about this stuff, for the reasons that, you know, they are engaging in these risky practices. So, yeah, interesting.
transcript.zh: 而且基本上他们认为，那些正在琢磨这些问题的实验室之所以去研究，是因为它们本身就在开展高风险实践，所以直接借鉴对方的最佳实践就行了。这很有意思。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So it's not that they're cavalier, necessarily, it's just that they have their focus on on very different things. It's that they're really focused on, you know, just improving their models because they're still behind, getting around compute constraints, and, you know, eventually making a little bit of money.
transcript.zh: 所以倒不一定是他们漫不经心，只是关注点完全不同。他们真正专注的，就是因为还处于落后而不断提升模型性能、绕过算力限制，以及最终赚到点真金白银。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Sounds very Chinese to me.
transcript.zh: 在我看来，这非常符合中国的行事风格。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: Yeah, exactly. Another thing is about the whole Effective Altruism movement, which is essentially the group of people who advocated for the x-risk, the catastrophic risk that could be induced by AI.
transcript.zh: 是的，没错。另一件事与整个“有效利他主义”运动有关，这群人本质上一直在鼓吹由人工智能可能引发的“生存风险”或灾难性风险。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: They are the ones who are just using some first-principle logic to speculate the future, and sometimes they could be very wrong. For example, they are the ones who would predict all the white-collar jobs, or like at least 50%, will be gone by this year or that year.
transcript.zh: 他们往往只凭借某些第一性原理的逻辑来推测未来，有时错得非常离谱。比如，正是他们预言所有白领岗位——或者至少50%——将在某年某月彻底消失。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: This is a very sort of logical prediction, but it is completely out of context because they never really added the cultural aspect into it, and never really considered that human society is a relational society.
transcript.zh: 这种推断虽然看似符合逻辑，但完全脱离了现实语境，因为他们从不把文化维度考虑在内，也从未真正意识到人类社会是一个关系型社会。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: So, they have a lot of blindness in their methodology, in their mental framework. I know many of them in Berkeley. I have a lot of friends who are EA, and sometimes they could be terribly wrong, sometimes they could be right, but there are definitely some flaws in the fundamental way they think about the world.
transcript.zh: 因此，在他们的方法论和思维框架中存在着巨大的盲区。我在伯克利认识很多这样的人，也有不少朋友信奉有效利他主义。他们有时错得离谱，有时也能言中，但在看待这个世界的基本方式上，绝对存在某些硬伤。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: What a surprise! Anyway, it's a wonderful couple of pieces, and I understand there's a third piece in the works in this trilogy now, and it's also going to be focused on Liangzhu, right? What is that one about?
transcript.zh: 毫不意外！不管怎么说，这两篇文章写得非常精彩。我知道这个三部曲中还有第三篇正在筹备，也是聚焦在良渚，对吧？那篇是关于什么的？

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: Yeah, the third piece is not necessarily focused on Liangzhu, but it does focus on what I call the industrial AI slop industry. It is essentially a phenomenon of this overwhelming amount of AI mini-dramas that are in a lot of people's timeline and produced by those studios located in a variety of parts of China.
transcript.zh: 第三篇倒不一定只聚焦良渚，但重点探讨的是被我称为“AI垃圾工业化”的产业。它本质上是指当下充斥在很多人信息流里、由分布在全国各地的短剧工作室批量炮制的泛滥成灾的AI短剧现象。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: I just really want to figure out what are the practices in those industries. Can we really create some original Chinese arts in those practices? Because I can see some renaissance in the AI content creation.
transcript.zh: 我只是非常想弄清楚这些行业内部的具体运作模式。我们真能从这些实践中创造出具有原创性的中国艺术吗？因为在AI内容创作领域，我确实能看到某种复兴的火花。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: But the more I dig in, the more I got slightly disappointed. Some people could argue that the Chinese AI mini-dramas could be a soft power export, but at the end, I think I made my own verdict. I said, well, it is not really soft culture when it is just slop.
transcript.zh: 但越往深处挖，我就越感到有些失望。有人或许会辩称中国AI短剧可以作为一种软实力出海，但在最后，我想我给出了自己的定论：如果它充其量只是垃圾内容，那就根本谈不上什么软实力文化。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Pure slop. Anyway, dear listeners, you should definitely read these couple of pieces of Afra's, and then of course look out for the one on the AI slop industry that will be coming down the pipeline.
transcript.zh: 纯粹的垃圾。总之，各位听众，你们一定要去读一读Afra写的这几篇文章，当然也要密切关注她即将推出的关于AI垃圾产业的最新力作。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: In these two pieces, she already introduces us to so many interesting folks. There's Casey, this kid barely out of his teens who's teaching his friends to vibe code in his living room there in Liangzhu. There's a woman called H who quit Tencent—she's like 27—to just explore ways of...
transcript.zh: 在这两篇文章中，她已经为我们引荐了许多极具特色的人物：比如刚满二十岁的年轻人Casey，他在良渚自家的客厅里教朋友们写“氛围代码”（vibe coding）；还有一位化名为H的女士，27岁就从腾讯离职，只为探索新的可能性……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: not going to work, which is sort of how I live my life. Her feed is just all flying lessons and Muay Thai in Chiang Mai. There's Xiao Kai, of course, we talked about the AI filmmaker from Dongbei.
transcript.zh: 不去打卡上班，这其实也是我习惯的生活状态。她的社媒动态里全是清迈的飞行课和泰拳训练。当然还有小凯，我们之前聊过的那位来自东北的 AI 电影创作者。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: You got that security guard, you got Levi, you got all these people in this piece, and that's one of the things that makes your writing so enjoyable is that there are these people who very much come to life in your prose, and I feel like I've met them as well.
transcript.zh: 你写到了那个保安，写到了 Levi，文章里充盈着这些鲜活的人物。这也正是你的文字读来引人入胜之处——这些人在你的笔下跃然纸上，仿佛我也与他们面对面交谈过一样。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: Oh, thank you. Thank you.
transcript.zh: 噢，谢谢，非常感谢！

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, I really urge everyone to read these stories and to subscribe to Afra's Concurrent Substack for more great writing from her. Before we say goodbye, we've got paying it forward and recommendations.
transcript.zh: 是的，我非常推荐大家去读这几篇报道，并订阅 Afra 的 Substack 专栏《Concurrent》，阅读更多她的精彩文章。在说再见之前，我们照例要进行“爱心传递”致敬环节和好物推荐。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Afra, I think you're about to, you're vying with Kyle Chan for being the most paid forward person on the show already. So I'm really curious who you would nominate for paying it forward this week.
transcript.zh: Afra，我觉得你现在都快赶上 Kyle Chan 了，成为节目里被别人致敬提及次数最多的嘉宾。所以这周我特别好奇，你想要向哪位同行致敬？

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: The first name I want to mention is Zulan Qian. I think for those who are curious about the AI safety discourse in the US and China, I think Zulan is a must read.
transcript.zh: 我首先想提到的是 Zulan Qian。我觉得对于那些对中美两国的 AI 安全议题和话语体系感兴趣的人来说，Zulan 的文章是必读的。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: I think she has the ability to really map some of the semantics, some of the terminologies into the Chinese context. For example, what does loss control mean in the Chinese context?
transcript.zh: 她非常擅长将一些语义和专业术语准确映射到中文语境中。例如，“失控”（Loss of Control）在中文语境下到底意味着什么？

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: Like, lost control by who, right? Like she would write a piece to explain that.
transcript.zh: 比如，究竟是谁的失控？对吧？她专门写过一篇文章来深入拆解这个概念。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Where does she write?
transcript.zh: 她在哪里发表文章？

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: She has her Substack, and she's also GovAI fellow now, research about AI governance in China. She would write something like, the most memorable and well-spread piece is why the US builds AI girlfriend and China builds AI boyfriend.
transcript.zh: 她有自己的 Substack 专栏，目前也是 GovAI 的研究员，专注于中国 AI 治理研究。她写过很多深度文章，其中最令人印象深刻、传播最广的一篇是分析《为什么美国在做 AI 女友，而中国在做 AI 男友》。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: Yeah, it's a phenomenon piece. But later, China banned the practice of anthropomorphizing AI.
transcript.zh: 是的，那是一篇现象级的文章。不过后来中国出台规定，限制了对 AI 进行过度拟人化的做法。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah. Zulan Qian, I'll definitely check her out. I don't think I've come across her stuff before. That sounds really great, right up my alley.
transcript.zh: 好的，Zulan Qian，我一定会去拜读她的作品。我之前好像还没拜读过她的文章，听上去非常棒，完全符合我的胃口。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: All right. Let's move on to recommendations. What do you have for recommendations for us this week?
transcript.zh: 好，那我们进入好物推荐环节。本周你有什么想向大家推荐的吗？

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: I've been reading Ken Liu recently, because I met him the past weekend at the CURVE conference.
transcript.zh: 我最近一直在读刘宇昆（Ken Liu）的作品，因为我上周末刚在 CURVE 大会上碰到了他。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, I heard you spent like 3 hours chatting away with him. Yeah.
transcript.zh: 对，我听说你跟他相谈甚欢，畅聊了大概三个小时。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: Yeah, I just spent some meaningful time chatting with Ken. Chatting a lot about the practice of AI art creation.
transcript.zh: 对，我和 Ken 进行了一次非常充实而有意义的交流。我们聊了很多关于 AI 艺术创作实践的内容。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: Ken is one of the most thoughtful writers or thinking about this subject when majority of the writers are not very even interested in thinking about this seriously, you know, like many of them just condescendingly say...
transcript.zh: 在大多数作家甚至都不屑于认真思考这个议题，或者只是居高临下地予以否定的时候，Ken 是极少数对这个话题有着极其深刻、周全思考的作家之一。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Let me quickly ID Ken for people who don't know who he is. He is a science fiction writer. He wrote an interesting series of books, a genre that he's called silkpunk.
transcript.zh: 我来向不熟悉 Ken 的听众快速介绍一下。他就是著名科幻作家刘宇昆。他创作了一部非常引人入胜的系列小说，开创了他称之为“丝绸朋克”（Silkpunk）的全新流派。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: Silkpunk.
transcript.zh: 丝绸朋克。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, and it's actually about the Chu-Han Contention.
transcript.zh: 是的，那部作品实际上是以楚汉相争的历史为灵感架构的。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: an imagined universe based on silkpunk technology. And he is also, of course, the translator of Liu Cixin's Three-Body Problem trilogy—the first book, The Three-Body Problem itself, and the third book in that trilogy were his translations.
transcript.zh: 设定在一个基于“丝绸朋克”技术的虚构宇宙中。当然，他也是刘慈欣《三体》三部曲的译者——第一部《三体》和第三部都是由他翻译的。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: They're excellent. I interviewed him on Sinica some years ago. Really interesting guy.
transcript.zh: 译本非常出色。几年前我在 Sinica 采访过他，他是个非常有意思的人。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: Yeah, he has a new anthology coming out called The Passing of the Dragon. And the dragon is actually a metaphor created by Ursula Le Guin, a renowned sci-fi writer both Ken and I seen as idol.
transcript.zh: 对，他最近有一部新的作品集即将出版，叫《飞龙之逝》（The Passing of the Dragon）。这里的“龙”实际上是一个隐喻，出自著名科幻作家 Ursula Le Guin，我和 Ken 都把她视为偶像。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: I personally paid some pilgrimage to Le Guin's old house when I was visiting Portland. I was walking on the beach that inspired her to write the Earthsea series. I was properly fangirling Ursula Le Guin, and walking on the road she walked before.
transcript.zh: 我去波特兰的时候，还特意去 Le Guin 的故居朝圣。我走在曾启发她创作《地海传奇》（Earthsea）系列的海滩上，简直就像个狂热的迷妹，走着她当年走过的路。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: You might know her—I think grandson or grandnephew, Arthur Kroeber, the well-known economist of Gavekal Dragonomics. You've probably run into him, you know, as we run into so much folks.
transcript.zh: 你可能知道她的孙子或者侄孙，也就是龙洲经讯（Gavekal Dragonomics）的知名经济学家 Arthur Kroeber。你可能见过他，毕竟我们圈子里的人经常碰面。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: I recognized the last name because Le Guin's maiden name is Kroeber. So I asked Arthur, and Arthur nodded, and my mind just exploded at the moment. It's such a beautiful and interesting and magical connection in this world.
transcript.zh: 我认出了这个姓氏，因为 Le Guin 的娘家姓就是 Kroeber。我去问 Arthur，他点头确认了，我当时整个人都惊呆了。这在这个世界上真是一种美妙、有趣又神奇的缘分。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, she's... I know my brother is a diehard science fiction reader, and his favorite author is Ursula Le Guin, so. Yeah, Ken Liu though, back to Ken. That's interesting. So he's got a new anthology coming out, The Passing of the Dragon, and the dragon is a metaphor from Ursula Le Guin. A metaphor for what?
transcript.zh: 我哥哥也是个狂热的科幻小说迷，他最喜欢的作者就是 Ursula Le Guin。不过说回 Ken Liu，这很有意思，他要出一本新选集《飞龙之逝》，而“龙”是来自 Ursula Le Guin 的隐喻。它隐喻的是什么呢？

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: It is a metaphor for... I guess it is a little bit abstract, but my understanding is it is a certain story or certain truth. It is pretty Daoism, to be honest. I do think Le Guin and Ken are very Daoist in terms of their storytelling.
transcript.zh: 它是对……我想这有点抽象，但在我看来，它指的是某种故事或某种真理。坦率地说，这非常具有道家思想的意味。我认为 Le Guin 和 Ken 在讲故事方面都非常具有道家风范。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: This dragon is something that's undescribable, some sublimity. But they're trying to use their words to lay down some prints, some trace, so the readers can have a sense of what the dragon might look like. I guess it is somewhat abstract, but it makes perfect sense to me because I'm also really into fictional writing.
transcript.zh: 这条“龙”是某种不可言说之物，某种崇高的存在。但他们试图用文字留下一些脚印、一些痕迹，让读者能感知到这条龙大概长什么样。我想这确实有点抽象，但对我来说完全能理解，因为我自己也沉迷于虚构写作。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: Ken described it much better in his interview, so go check out Ken's book talk. Yeah, he described it much better.
transcript.zh: Ken 在他的访谈里阐述得好得多，大家可以去听听 Ken 的新书分享会。是的，他解释得透彻得多。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Fantastic. Okay, great recommendation. Mine for this week is the novel Home by Marilynne Robinson, which is the second book in the series of four that begins with the book Gilead.
transcript.zh: 太棒了。好的，非常棒的推荐。我本周的推荐是 Marilynne Robinson 的小说《家园》（Home），这是以《基列家书》（Gilead）为开篇的四部曲中的第二部。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: That is a book I've talked about at length on this show before. Um, this actually, this book, *Home*, focuses on characters who are present in *Gilead*, the novel, as well as Gilead, the eponymous fictional town in Iowa.
transcript.zh: 这是我之前在节目里详聊过的一本书。其实这本《家》（Home）聚焦于小说《基列家书》（Gilead）中出现过的人物，背景同样设在爱荷华州那个同名虚构小镇基列。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: The action takes place in the same time, the same few weeks as *Gilead*, but from a completely different perspective. So it's, you know, it's interesting, there's a little bit of *Rashomon* going on. It's a marvelous conceit, I actually think.
transcript.zh: 故事发生的时间与《基列家书》完全重合，就在相同的几周内，但视角截然不同。所以，你知道，这很有意思，有点《罗生门》的味道。我认为这是一个极其精妙的构思。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: The main character is Glory Boughton. She's the youngest daughter—in a big family of eight kids—of the Presbyterian minister who is best friends with the protagonist of *Gilead*, the novel. So she's come home in her late 30s after a broken engagement with a married man who's been like siphoning money off her.
transcript.zh: 主角是 Glory Boughton。她是长老会牧师家八个孩子里最小的女儿，而这位牧师正是《基列家书》主角的挚友。她在三十大几岁时回到了家，之前刚解除婚约，对方是个已婚男人，一直在榨取她的钱财。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And it happens that her older brother Jack, who features very prominently in *Gilead*—this Jack has a troubled childhood, the prodigal son. He's left home for a long time, no one's heard from him.
transcript.zh: 巧合的是，在《基列家书》中极为显眼的长兄 Jack 也回来了——这个 Jack 童年坎坷，是个典型的浪子。他离家多年，杳无音讯。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: He has a lot of charm. He's abundantly charming and quite erudite, but he's got a very bad reputation, which he's mostly earned. He's come home too. So it's the two of them.
transcript.zh: 他魅力十足，不仅风度翩翩而且颇为博学，但声名狼藉——而这多半也是他咎由自取。他也回到了家，于是家里就剩他们兄妹二人。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And it's set against, you know, the backdrop of the United States in the mid-1950s, 1956 specifically. So Eisenhower's America, the election of '56, the Suez Crisis, the Montgomery bus boycott, and the aftermath of the murder of Emmett Till—it's all in there in the backdrop.
transcript.zh: 小说的时代背景是20世纪50年代中期的美国，具体是1956年。也就是艾森豪威尔时期的美国，1956年大选、苏伊士运河危机、蒙哥马利巴士抵制运动，以及 Emmett Till 遇害案的余波——所有这些都构成了故事的时代底色。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And it turns out to matter really enormously, because Jack has a secret that the whole novel kind of circles around without quite naming it until nearly the end. Much of the book is just really the two siblings having coffee in their kitchen, you know, in this big, creaking house, tending to their dying father and trying to figure out how much they can trust each other and what they can say.
transcript.zh: 而这些背景其实至关重要，因为 Jack 身上藏着一个秘密，整部小说都在围绕它兜圈子，直到接近尾声才真正挑明。书里的大部分篇幅其实就是兄妹俩在这栋吱呀作响的老大宅厨房里喝咖啡，照顾奄奄一息的父亲，并试图探寻彼此能给予多少信任、能说出多少真话。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And it's really great. Marilynne Robinson is just one of those writers whose prose is luminous, but super plain. It's so unadorned. I just wish I could write like that.
transcript.zh: 这本书非常棒。Marilynne Robinson 就是那种文笔清澈如光芒流淌、却又极其质朴的作家。文字洗尽铅华。我真希望自己也能写出那样的文字。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: It makes something so quotidian as, you know, eating pancakes at the old kitchen table and the conversation that happens, just feel like the most consequential thing in the world. And it's actually a sadder book than *Gilead*.
transcript.zh: 她能让围在旧厨房餐桌旁吃煎饼、闲聊这样无比日常的事情，显得像是全世界最生死攸关的大事。实际上，它比《基列家书》还要更伤感。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: *Gilead* has got a lot of sadness in it, but this is really kind of pretty devastating in a lot of ways. But it really rewards if you read the two of them together. If you've read *Gilead*—I know a lot of my friends, for some reason, it was in the air, a lot of people started reading *Gilead* over the summer. So this is definitely the one to pick up next.
transcript.zh: 《基列家书》固然有很多悲凉，但这本在很多层面上简直让人心碎。不过两本书对照着读确实会获益良多。如果你已经读过《基列家书》——我知道身边的很多朋友不知怎的，好像赶上了某种潮流，夏天很多人都开始读《基列家书》。那么接下来的下一本绝对非它莫属。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: Hmm. Yeah. Reminds me of—J.G. Ballard has an essay talking about this importance of mediocrity and the invisible literature about this bureaucratic, using like this bureaucratic language.
transcript.zh: 嗯，对。这让我想起 J.G. Ballard 曾写过一篇散文，谈到平庸之物的重要性，以及运用这种官僚化语言所书写的隐形文学。

transcript.speaker: Afra Wang
transcript.en: To write stories, I think there is like this... It shows some craft, right? This quotidian description of the world, but like somewhat profound, it shows some powerful craft.
transcript.zh: 去写故事，我觉得有这样一种……这展现了一种笔力，对吧？这种对世界日常琐碎的白描，却能透出某种深刻，展现出非常强大的写作功力。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Oh, for sure. I mean, that's sort of been a theme for me this whole summer. I mean, that's how I fell in love with John Williams over the summer. And if you've read the book—I've talked about it so much—Stoner, it's these like small, seemingly low-stakes stories of ordinary, ordinary people.
transcript.zh: 噢，确实如此。这可以说是贯穿我整个夏天的阅读主题。我就是在这个夏天迷上了 John Williams。如果你读过那本我反复提起的《斯通纳》（Stoner），就会发现写的就是这些看似微不足道、微小的普通人故事。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
